claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
A uniform sub-micron Al2O3 coating can be deposited on the alloy by PVD or ALD.
Depositing an Al2O3 coating will significantly improve the oxidation resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr in high-temperature air.
The Al2O3 coating will not degrade the alloy's intrinsic room-temperature mechanical properties.
The Al2O3 coating will not degrade the alloy's intrinsic high-temperature mechanical properties.
The coating will form a continuous sub-micron diffusion barrier over the alloy surface.
The Al2O3 layer will impede oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Impeding oxygen transport will inhibit formation and spallation of nonprotective oxide scales.
The coating will prevent or minimize pesting during approximately 5 hours in air at 800–1000 °C.
A sub-micron surface coating will leave the bulk alloy microstructure essentially unaltered.
Preserving the bulk microstructure will preserve the alloy's mechanical performance.
Relative to untreated samples, coated samples will have lower oxidation mass gain or a thinner oxide scale.
Relative to untreated samples, coated samples will retain their characteristic room-temperature ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes significant oxygen uptake and pesting during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800–1000 °C.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between the Al2O3 coating and substrate could cause coating cracking or spallation.
The proposed test compares coated and uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr under identical 900 °C, 5-hour air exposures.
Failure to reduce oxidation or significant deterioration of mechanical properties relative to the uncoated control would falsify the hypothesis.
